title: Learning to Cook Cantonese Food with My Grandma

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: hello, welcome to my channel. my name is angela. and today i'm doing a little bit of a different video. instead of my normal vlogs, i'm going to be learning how to cook for my grandma. because since i moved to montreal, i haven't really gotten to eat a lot of the comfort foods that i grew up eating. and so i want to learn how to cook them so that when i'm back in montreal, i can cook them for myself. so today, because my grandma speaks in cantonese, this video is also going to be a little bit different because i'm going to try to speak cantonese for the rest of the video. my cantonese is not very good because i grew up in canada, but i will put english subtitles here for you if you don't speak cantonese. but yeah, let's get started. so, today my grandma will be teaching me how to cook chinese soap, stir-fried vegetables. braised ribs with dried beancurd sticks. okay, let's get started. first, what should we do ..grandma ?.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Hello Angela, I'm so happy to see you wanting to learn our family recipes! Let's start with the Chinese soup. First, we need to gather all the ingredients. Do you have them ready?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Yes, I have everything ready! I'm really excited to learn from you. What's the first step?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Ah, for the dried beancurd sticks, you should soak them for about 30 minutes until they become soft. It's important to make sure they're fully soaked before cooking. Do you have any other questions about the ingredients?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Thanks for the tip, Grandma! I'll make sure to soak them properly. I think I'm good with the ingredients for now. What's the next step after soaking the beancurd sticks?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yes, that's right! Following the bones is a good way to cut the ribs. It helps you get nice, even pieces. You're doing great, Angela! Do you need any more tips?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Wait, I didn't ask about cutting ribs yet. You interrupted my question about the next step after soaking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I didn't interrupt. I was answering your question. Cutting ribs is the next step.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: But I was still speaking. You jumped in before I finished my sentence.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You paused after 'soaking.' I thought you were done. In Cantonese conversation, we fill pauses quickly.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm speaking English. A pause doesn't mean I'm done. It means I'm thinking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Thinking looks like finished to me. I was trying to be helpful by answering early.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Helpful would be waiting until I finish my question. Now I don't know if you skipped a step.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I didn't skip. Soak first, then cut ribs. I was giving you the roadmap.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: By talking over me? That's not a roadmap. That's a detour.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm guiding you. Like a GPS.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: GPS waits for you to ask before giving directions. It doesn't interrupt mid-question.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: GPS is a machine. I'm a person. People overlap.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: People also listen. You're not listening.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I am listening. I just anticipate. It's a sign of attention.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Anticipation while I'm speaking feels like dismissal. Like my words don't matter.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your words matter. That's why I want to answer them quickly.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Quick answers to unfinished questions are wrong answers.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The answer was correct. Cut ribs after soaking.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: But what if I was going to ask about the water temperature? You assumed I was asking about ribs.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Were you going to ask about temperature?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: No, but I could have. And you would have answered the wrong thing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: This is very complicated. In my kitchen, we just cook. We don't analyze every pause.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: In my kitchen, we need clarity. Otherwise the food doesn't turn out.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The food will turn out. Trust the process. Trust me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I want to trust you. But I also need to trust that you'll let me finish my sentences.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I will try. But my trying might look like failing to you.
